authority: E2E-REPORT.md §5 (2026-10-22; source retained in private lane acceptance evidence); version-sensitive publication wording follows HEAD strict/permissive contract

text.python_nonregular_sources: **Accounted non-regular-source difference (Release A).** FIFOs and device files are outside the Python captured-`File` admission contract. On Linux, `oxblend summary /dev/null` refuses with `truncated` / `range 0+7 exceeds 0 bytes`, while `oxblend.open("/dev/null")` (and Python `summary`) refuses before opening the device with `pack_path` / `pack source is not regular file`. No FIFO/device special case, capture-policy widening or general canonical-error exception is implied. Ordinary admitted file errors retain canonical parity; this specific CLI-versus-Session difference is pinned separately. A shared non-regular-source policy remains follow-up work.
text.diagnosis: **Diagnose does not mean repair.** `inspect`, `get`, `pointer` and `payload` describe saved bytes; they do not establish the intended scene. If trace or pack reports an invalid/unknown pointer, explain the site and stop. Do not guess a replacement pointer, null it, or bypass an Oxblend refusal with Python, hex editing or another writer unless the user explicitly authorizes a separate repair plan. Keep the original untouched. A clean trace or `complete:true` after a change proves only this command's serialized contract, not that the change is correct or that Blender can open or render it. Prefer a known-good save or repair in compatible Blender, then verify the new file natively before recommending delivery.
text.validation: Dependency package status: COMPLETE / INCOMPLETE (see report). “Complete” concerns the selected serialized dependency closure only. Blender open, evaluation and rendering have NOT been verified by this command. Before farm delivery, open the isolated package in compatible Blender with original project sources unavailable; check missing data and run the required render checks. A repaired or byte-edited input needs its own native validation.
text.metadata: `summary` supplies every saved Scene's range and FPS, but this version does not include render output paths. Save `oxblend inspect FILE`, find every `SC` block (ASCII code bytes with NUL padding), and for each element run `oxblend get FILE BLOCK '["r","pic"]' ELEMENT`. `BLOCK` and element count come from this exact input; never reuse the example's indices. Decode `value.hex` as the saved path bytes. `//` is relative to the owning blend file, not the shell's working directory. Report both the saved spelling and its resolution, and label native/evaluated output behavior unverified.
text.inspect: `inspect.blocks` is an ordered array: its array index is BLOCK. `code_hex` includes all four code bytes, including NUL padding; Scene is `53430000`, not `5343`. Addresses are in `address_decimal`; parse decimal strings as integers before numeric formatting. Struct names are obtained from the SDNA type/struct tables. Read an actual saved record before selecting field names; do not assume `index`, `code`, `type`, `source_path` or `destination_path` aliases.
text.report: On refusal, retain stdout, stderr and exit status. Run `oxblend help error KIND` for every nested causal kind. Save the complete final schema-1 JSON stderr envelope (not mixed diagnostic prose): it includes an invocation receipt even when tracing is off. `oxblend report --report failure.json --stdout saved.stdout --output bug.zip --preview` verifies saved stdout and the canonical original error-envelope digest. With tracing, pass `--trace TRACE.jsonl`, or explicitly select `--run-id ID` / `--last` within `--trace-dir LOCAL_DIR`. The receipt binds the exact trace/root-span identity; legacy or interrupted evidence remains unverified/unknown. Incomplete stdout delivery stays explicitly partial even when its accepted-byte digest matches. A legacy/unrelated saved report never inherits verification from another trace. Review every returned member and privacy warning, then publish only that snapshot with `report --create PREVIEW.json --preview-sha256 SHA256 --output bug.zip`. Names, paths, raw messages, argv, payload and scene bytes are excluded by default; typed identifiers are bundle-local HMAC-SHA-256 tokens. Never add `--include-names` or `--include-file FILE` without an explicit informed choice; whole-file opt-in discloses all contents as a user-supplied, unverified attachment, not a certified input scene. Only accept a preview obtained directly from your own report command; create publishes caller-reviewed bytes but does not authenticate or re-sanitize a preview+digest supplied by another party. The CLI never reruns the failed command, recaptures source files, launches a browser, uploads or files. Show the fixed public GitHub prefill and reviewed local ZIP to the user; filing and attachment remain manual. Reporting does not repair or validate a scene.
text.run_helper: `run LABEL COMMAND [ARGS...]` uses LABEL only for log filenames; COMMAND is still required. Correct: `run overview summary scene.blend`. Incorrect: `run summary scene.blend`. The helper is a shell function, not an executable: put optional launch wrappers around `$OXBLEND` inside the function, not around `run`. Direct `oxblend … >stdout 2>stderr; status=$?` calls are equally valid.
text.release: `cargo install oxblend --locked` installs the released crate, not GitHub main. After installation run `oxblend --version`, then `oxblend skill` for its matching offline guide. Use documentation for that exact version. Examples for an unreleased build do not imply that its flags exist in the released CLI. Checkout links stay main-relative until a matching release tag exists.
